definition: To publicly recommend, support, or urge for a particular policy, cause, or course of action.
definition_zh: 擁護；提倡；主張

mnemonic.story_en: The activist went to AD (to) the stage to VOC (call) upon the citizens to ADVOCATE for environmental protection.
mnemonic.story_zh: 抗議者走向（AD）舞台大聲呼喊（VOC），呼籲市民一同「提倡（ADVOCATE）」環保。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD = to, toward; connect this root idea with advocate.

example: Many economists advocate introducing a carbon tax to tackle climate change globally.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 advocate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: champion is related, but advocate has its own usage pattern and context.
support may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with advocate.

usage_note: advocate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Open to more than one interpretation, or having a double meaning, often causing confusion or uncertainty.
definition_zh: 含糊不清的；引起歧義的；模稜兩可的

mnemonic.story_en: The sign was AMBI (both) ways, which IG (drove) drivers to make AMBIGUOUS decisions at the intersection.
mnemonic.story_zh: 指標同時指向兩邊（AMBI），這驅使（IG）駕駛在十字路口做出「模稜兩可的（AMBIGUOUS）」決定。
mnemonic.root_memory: AMBI = both, around; connect this root idea with ambiguous.

example: The legislation was deliberately left ambiguous to allow for future political compromises.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 ambiguous 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: equivocal is related, but ambiguous has its own usage pattern and context.
vague may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with ambiguous.

usage_note: ambiguous is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To regard something as being caused by, or belonging to, a specific person, thing, or source.
definition_zh: 歸因於；歸功於；認為…是某人所做

mnemonic.story_en: The scholars AD (to) tribute to the master and ATTRIBUTE the discovery entirely to his guidance.
mnemonic.story_zh: 學者們向（AD）大師致敬，並將（TRIBUT）這項發現「歸功於（ATTRIBUTE）」他的指導。
mnemonic.root_memory: AD = to, toward; connect this root idea with attribute.

example: Scientists attribute the recent increase in extreme weather events to global warming.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 attribute 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: ascribe is related, but attribute has its own usage pattern and context.
credit may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with attribute.

usage_note: attribute is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Existing or acting independently; having the freedom and authority to govern itself or control its own affairs.
definition_zh: 自治的；自主的；獨立自主的

mnemonic.story_en: An AUTO (self) governing region makes its own NOMOS (laws) to remain fully AUTONOMOUS from the empire.
mnemonic.story_zh: 一個自我（AUTO）治理的地區建立了自己的法律（NOMOS），以保持完全「自治的（AUTONOMOUS）」狀態。
mnemonic.root_memory: AUTO = self; connect this root idea with autonomous.

example: The university's research departments operate as autonomous units with their own budgets.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 autonomous 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: independent is related, but autonomous has its own usage pattern and context.
sovereign may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with autonomous.

usage_note: autonomous is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Logical, orderly, and consistent; clear and easy to understand because all parts fit together well.
definition_zh: 連貫的；條理分明的；前後一致的

mnemonic.story_en: When all paragraphs CO (together) HER (stick), the essay becomes a COHERENT argument.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當所有段落都緊密「黏（HER）」在「一起（CO）」時，這篇論文就成了一個「連貫的（COHERENT）」論證。
mnemonic.root_memory: CO = together; connect this root idea with coherent.

example: The minister failed to provide a coherent explanation for the sudden policy shift.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 coherent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: logical is related, but coherent has its own usage pattern and context.
consistent may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with coherent.

usage_note: coherent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To give someone something, typically money, in recognition of loss, suffering, or injury; or to act to neutralize an adverse effect.
definition_zh: 補償；賠償；彌補

mnemonic.story_en: The judge will weigh COM (together) the damages and the PENS (payment) to COMPENSATE the victim.
mnemonic.story_zh: 法官將受損部分與支付款（PENS）放在「一起（COM）」稱重衡量，以「補償（COMPENSATE）」受害者。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM = together, thoroughly; connect this root idea with compensate.

example: The company agreed to compensate the workers for the additional hours they worked during the holiday.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 compensate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: reimburse is related, but compensate has its own usage pattern and context.
indemnify may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with compensate.

usage_note: compensate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To add to something in a way that enhances or improves it; to make something perfect or complete.
definition_zh: 補充；與…相輔相成；使完美

mnemonic.story_en: The red wine was chosen to COM (completely) PLE (fill) the dinner, as it would COMPLEMENT the steak perfectly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 選擇這款紅酒是為了「完全（COM）填滿（PLE）」這頓晚宴，因為它能與牛排「相輔相成（COMPLEMENT）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM = together, completely; connect this root idea with complement.

example: The husband's calm demeanor complements his wife's energetic personality perfectly.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 complement 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: supplement is related, but complement has its own usage pattern and context.
enhance may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with complement.

usage_note: complement is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Complete; including all or nearly all elements, aspects, or items of something.
definition_zh: 全面的；廣泛的；包羅萬象的

mnemonic.story_en: The guide will COM (together) PREHENS (seize) all facts to provide a COMPREHENSIVE overview of the museum.
mnemonic.story_zh: 導覽員將把所有事實「抓（PREHENS）」在「一起（COM）」，以提供對博物館「全面的（COMPREHENSIVE）」概述。
mnemonic.root_memory: COM = together; connect this root idea with comprehensive.

example: The insurance policy provides comprehensive coverage against fire, theft, and natural disasters.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 comprehensive 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: exhaustive is related, but comprehensive has its own usage pattern and context.
thorough may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with comprehensive.

usage_note: comprehensive is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Making a certain situation or outcome likely or possible; contributing to a desirable result.
definition_zh: 有助於…的；促成…的

mnemonic.story_en: Quiet environments CON (together) DUC (lead) minds to focus, making them CONDUCIVE to deep study.
mnemonic.story_zh: 安靜的環境會「引導（DUC）」思緒凝聚在「一起（CON）」，這使其「有助於（CONDUCIVE）」深度學習。
mnemonic.root_memory: CON = together; connect this root idea with conducive.

example: The noisy open-plan office is not particularly conducive to intensive research or creative writing.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 conducive 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: favorable is related, but conducive has its own usage pattern and context.
beneficial may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with conducive.

usage_note: conducive is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Giving rise or likely to give rise to public disagreement, heated debate, or conflicting opinions.
definition_zh: 有爭議的；引發爭論的

mnemonic.story_en: When a topic forces opinions to turn VERS (turn) CONTRA (against) each other, it becomes CONTROVERSIAL.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當一個議題迫使觀點「轉向（VERS）」彼此「相反（CONTRA）」的立場時，它就成了「有爭議的（CONTROVERSIAL）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: CONTRA = against, opposite; connect this root idea with controversial.

example: The decision to build a nuclear power plant near the coastline remains highly controversial.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 controversial 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: disputed is related, but controversial has its own usage pattern and context.
contentious may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with controversial.

usage_note: controversial is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A mutual relationship or connection between two or more things, where a change in one is associated with a change in the other.
definition_zh: 相關性；相互關係

mnemonic.story_en: Scientists study how two variables are COR (together) RELAT (related) to establish a clear CORRELATION.
mnemonic.story_zh: 科學家研究兩個變數是如何「聯繫（RELAT）」在「一起（COR）」的，以建立明確的「相關性（CORRELATION）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: COR = together; connect this root idea with correlation.

example: Statistical evidence shows a strong correlation between high sugar consumption and obesity rates.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 correlation 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: connection is related, but correlation has its own usage pattern and context.
link may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with correlation.

usage_note: correlation is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Not having enough of a specified quality or ingredient; lacking in something necessary.
definition_zh: 缺乏的；不足的；有缺陷的

mnemonic.story_en: Because the chef did DE (down) FIC (make) the prep work, the soup was DEFICIENT in salt.
mnemonic.story_zh: 因為廚師做（FIC）得太少、往下掉（DE），導致這道湯在鹽分上顯得「缺乏的（DEFICIENT）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: DE = down, away from; connect this root idea with deficient.

example: A diet deficient in vitamin D can lead to severe bone weakness over time.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 deficient 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: lacking is related, but deficient has its own usage pattern and context.
insufficient may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with deficient.

usage_note: deficient is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To show clearly by giving proof, evidence, or examples; or to explain how something works by operating it.
definition_zh: 證明；證實；示範；展示

mnemonic.story_en: The engineer will DE (completely) MONSTR (show) the blueprint to DEMONSTRATE the safety of the bridge.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工程師將「徹底（DE）展示（MONSTR）」藍圖，以「證明（DEMONSTRATE）」橋樑的安全性。
mnemonic.root_memory: DE = completely, thoroughly; connect this root idea with demonstrate.

example: The laboratory experiment successfully demonstrated the law of conservation of energy.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 demonstrate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: prove is related, but demonstrate has its own usage pattern and context.
illustrate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with demonstrate.

usage_note: demonstrate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make or become less, smaller, or weaker in size, extent, or importance.
definition_zh: 減少；變小；削弱；貶低

mnemonic.story_en: As resources go DE (down), the team must MIN (make small) expenses to prevent power from being DIMINISHED.
mnemonic.story_zh: 隨著資源下滑（DE），團隊必須「變小（MIN）」開支，以防止力量被「削弱（DIMINISHED）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: DE = completely, down; connect this root idea with diminish.

example: The medication helped to diminish the severe pain in her joints within an hour.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 diminish 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: decrease is related, but diminish has its own usage pattern and context.
dwindle may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with diminish.

usage_note: diminish is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex; or the ability to perceive fine distinctions.
definition_zh: 歧視；不公正對待；辨別力；識別

mnemonic.story_en: To sift DIS (apart) groups based on bias is to CRIM (separate) them unlawfully, creating DISCRIMINATION.
mnemonic.story_zh: 基於偏見將群體「分開（DIS）」並「篩選對待（CRIM）」，就會造成「歧視（DISCRIMINATION）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: DIS = apart, away; connect this root idea with discrimination.

example: The civil rights organization fought tirelessly against racial discrimination in housing markets.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 discrimination 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: prejudice is related, but discrimination has its own usage pattern and context.
bias may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with discrimination.

usage_note: discrimination is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Based on, concerned with, or verifiable by observation or experience rather than theory or pure logic.
definition_zh: 經驗主義的；以觀察或實驗為依據的；實證的

mnemonic.story_en: The scientist put EM (in) action a fresh PEIRA (trial) to gather solid EMPIRICAL data.
mnemonic.story_zh: 科學家將新的「嘗試（PEIRA）」投入「其中（EM）」，以此來收集扎實的「實證（EMPIRICAL）」數據。
mnemonic.root_memory: EN / EM = in, into; connect this root idea with empirical.

example: The professor presented empirical evidence derived from a ten-year study to support his hypothesis.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 empirical 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: observational is related, but empirical has its own usage pattern and context.
experimental may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with empirical.

usage_note: empirical is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Equal in value, amount, function, meaning, or importance, though not necessarily identical in form.
definition_zh: 等值的；相等的；等價的；相對應的物

mnemonic.story_en: Two currencies with EQUI (equal) VAL (value) are considered completely EQUIVALENT in global trade.
mnemonic.story_zh: 兩種擁有「相等（EQUI）」「價值（VAL）」的貨幣，在全球貿易中被視為完全「等值的（EQUIVALENT）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: EQUI = equal; connect this root idea with equivalent.

example: Spreading rumors online is the moral equivalent of whispering behind someone's back.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 equivalent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: identical is related, but equivalent has its own usage pattern and context.
comparable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with equivalent.

usage_note: equivalent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To form an idea of the amount, number, value, or quality of something after careful appraisal.
definition_zh: 評估；評價；估價

mnemonic.story_en: Experts work to bring E (out) the real VALU (worth) of the asset to EVALUATE its market potential.
mnemonic.story_zh: 專家致力於將資產的「價值（VALU）」推導「出來（E）」，以此來「評估（EVALUATE）」其市場潛力。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX / E = out; connect this root idea with evaluate.

example: The committee will thoroughly evaluate all research proposals before allocating the grant money.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 evaluate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: assess is related, but evaluate has its own usage pattern and context.
appraise may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with evaluate.

usage_note: evaluate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To represent something as being larger, better, worse, or more important than it really is.
definition_zh: 誇大；誇張；言過其實

mnemonic.story_en: Do not EX (thoroughly) aggerate the facts into a massive AGGER (heap) just to make the headline sound scary.
mnemonic.story_zh: 不要「徹底（EX）」把事實「堆積（AGGER）」成大山，只為了讓新聞標題聽起來很嚇人（誇大）。
mnemonic.root_memory: EX = thoroughly, out; connect this root idea with exaggerate.

example: The media tends to exaggerate the risks of minor side effects to generate more clicks.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 exaggerate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: overstate is related, but exaggerate has its own usage pattern and context.
magnify may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with exaggerate.

usage_note: exaggerate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Possible to do easily or conveniently; realistic and likely to be achieved or carried out successfully.
definition_zh: 可行的；行得通的；切實可行的

mnemonic.story_en: If a grand business plan is truly FEAS (doable), it is marked as a FEASIBLE project by the bank.
mnemonic.story_zh: 如果一個宏大的商業計劃是真正「可做（FEAS）」的，它就會被銀行標記為「可行的（FEASIBLE）」項目。
mnemonic.root_memory: FEAS / FAC / FACERE = to do, make; connect this root idea with feasible.

example: With current technology, building a permanent human base on the Moon is entirely feasible.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 feasible 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: viable is related, but feasible has its own usage pattern and context.
practicable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with feasible.

usage_note: feasible is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To rise and fall irregularly in amount, number, value, or intensity, especially over time or in response to changing conditions.
definition_zh: 波動；變動；上下起伏

mnemonic.root_memory: FLUCT / FLUERE = flow or wave; prices that fluctuate move like waves.
mnemonic.story_en: Stock prices FLUCTUATE like waves, rising and falling whenever new economic news flows into the market.
mnemonic.story_zh: 股價像波浪（FLUCT）一樣隨著經濟消息流入市場而上下「波動（FLUCTUATE）」。

example: Exchange rates can fluctuate sharply when investors react to unexpected political news.
example_zh: 當投資人對突發政治消息做出反應時，匯率可能劇烈波動。

near_synonyms.difference: vary means to be different or change; fluctuate specifically suggests repeated rises and falls.
oscillate is often more regular or technical; fluctuate can be irregular and economic.

usage_note: Fluctuate is commonly used with prices, rates, temperatures, demand, and emotions.

definition: A system or organization in which people or groups are ranked one above another according to status, power, or authority.
definition_zh: 等級制度；階層；階級

mnemonic.story_en: In ancient times, HIERO (sacred) priests established an ARCHY (rule) to maintain a rigid social HIERARCHY.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在古代，神聖的（HIERO）祭司建立了一套統治體制（ARCHY），以維持嚴格的社會「等級制度（HIERARCHY）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: HIEROS = sacred, holy; connect this root idea with hierarchy.

example: In a traditional corporate hierarchy, major strategic decisions flow from top executives down to management.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 hierarchy 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: pecking order is related, but hierarchy has its own usage pattern and context.
ranking may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with hierarchy.

usage_note: hierarchy is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation or experimentation.
definition_zh: 假設；假說

mnemonic.story_en: Before a theory is built, a scientist lays a HYPO (under) statement beneath the THESIS (proposition) as a temporary HYPOTHESIS.
mnemonic.story_zh: 在建立正式理論前，科學家會在「核心論點（THESIS）」之「下（HYPO）」墊一個初步想法，作為暫時的「假設（HYPOTHESIS）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: HYPO = under, beneath; connect this root idea with hypothesis.

example: To test the hypothesis, the research team conducted a double-blind clinical study with over five hundred patients.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 hypothesis 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: supposition is related, but hypothesis has its own usage pattern and context.
theory may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with hypothesis.

usage_note: hypothesis is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To put a decision, plan, policy, or agreement into official effect or execution.
definition_zh: 實施；執行；貫徹

mnemonic.story_en: The manager will step IM (into) the project to PLE (fill) the gaps and IMPLEMENT the new safety protocol.
mnemonic.story_zh: 經理將介入（IM）項目中去填滿（PLE）漏洞，以「實施（IMPLEMENT）」新的安全協定。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN / IM = in, into; connect this root idea with implement.

example: The local government plans to implement stricter recycling regulations starting next month.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 implement 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: execute is related, but implement has its own usage pattern and context.
enact may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with implement.

usage_note: implement is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To strongly suggest the truth or existence of something without stating it directly or explicitly.
definition_zh: 暗示；暗指；意指；必然包含

mnemonic.story_en: He chose to fold his thoughts IM (in) a heavy PLY (fold), trying to IMPLY his displeasure without shouting.
mnemonic.story_zh: 他選擇把想法「摺疊（PLY）」在話語「內（IM）」，試圖以此「暗示（IMPLY）」他的不滿。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN / IM = in, into; connect this root idea with imply.

example: The study does not explicitly state that the drug is unsafe, but the data strongly implies it.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 imply 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: insinuate is related, but imply has its own usage pattern and context.
intimate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with imply.

usage_note: imply is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Something that incites or tends to incite to determination or action, such as a reward offered for increased productivity.
definition_zh: 激勵；刺激；動機；鼓勵之物

mnemonic.story_en: The general played a war song IN (into) the camp, using the tune as a financial INCENTIVE to spark bravery.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將軍在軍營「唱起（CENT）」戰歌注入（IN）士兵耳中，以此作為「激勵（INCENTIVE）」來激發勇氣。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN = into, upon; connect this root idea with incentive.

example: The government is offering tax incentives to encourage local families to install solar panels.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 incentive 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: inducement is related, but incentive has its own usage pattern and context.
motivation may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with incentive.

usage_note: incentive is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To take in or include something as a part of a larger whole, group, or system.
definition_zh: 納入；併入；將…合併；包含

mnemonic.story_en: The designer decided to build IN (into) the main CORPOR (body) of the dress a set of tech fibers to INCORPORATE style and safety.
mnemonic.story_zh: 設計師決定將科技纖維「注入（IN）」服裝的「主體（CORPOR）」中，以此來「結合（INCORPORATE）」時尚與安全。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN = into; connect this root idea with incorporate.

example: The new version of the software incorporates several features requested by users.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 incorporate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: integrate is related, but incorporate has its own usage pattern and context.
assimilate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with incorporate.

usage_note: incorporate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Certain to happen; unavoidable because of natural laws or logical sequence.
definition_zh: 不可避免的；必然發生的

mnemonic.story_en: It is IN (not) possible to run E (out) and VIT (avoid) aging; it is an INEVITABLE part of life.
mnemonic.story_zh: 人「不（IN）」可能逃「向外（E）」去「躲避（VIT）」老化；這是生命中「不可避免的（INEVITABLE）」一部分。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN = not; connect this root idea with inevitable.

example: With the bridge heavily collapsed, a massive traffic delay across the district became inevitable.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 inevitable 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: unavoidable is related, but inevitable has its own usage pattern and context.
inescapable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with inevitable.

usage_note: inevitable is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.
definition_zh: 基礎建設；基礎設施

mnemonic.story_en: Workers must build INFRA (below) the ground to set up the water STRUCT (structure) for the city's INFRASTRUCTURE.
mnemonic.story_zh: 工人必須在地面「之下（INFRA）」「建造（STRUCT）」供水管道，這構成了城市的「基礎建設（INFRASTRUCTURE）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: INFRA = below, underneath; connect this root idea with infrastructure.

example: Developing countries need substantial foreign investment to upgrade their aging transport infrastructure.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 infrastructure 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: substructure is related, but infrastructure has its own usage pattern and context.
foundation may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with infrastructure.

usage_note: infrastructure is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute; belonging by nature.
definition_zh: 固有的；內在的；生來就有的

mnemonic.story_en: The love for art was stuck IN (within) his mind, a trait that would HER (stick) as an INHERENT passion.
mnemonic.story_zh: 對藝術的熱愛「黏（HER）」在深處「內部（IN）」，這是他「固有的（INHERENT）」熱情。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN = in, within; connect this root idea with inherent.

example: Every financial investment in the stock market involves an inherent risk of losing capital.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 inherent 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: innate is related, but inherent has its own usage pattern and context.
intrinsic may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with inherent.

usage_note: inherent is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: The action or process of innovating; a new method, idea, or product brought forward.
definition_zh: 創新；革新；新觀念；新發明

mnemonic.story_en: The startup injected IN (into) the market a completely NOV (new) engine model, driving technological INNOVATION.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這家新創公司將全新（NOV）的引擎模式注入（IN）市場，推動了技術「創新（INNOVATION）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: IN = into, thoroughly; connect this root idea with innovation.

example: Continuous technological innovation is crucial for companies trying to survive in competitive markets.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 innovation 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: invention is related, but innovation has its own usage pattern and context.
novelty may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with innovation.

usage_note: innovation is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To combine one thing with another so that they become a whole, smooth, functioning system.
definition_zh: 整合；使合併；融入群體

mnemonic.story_en: To make the system INTEGR (whole), engineers must INTEGRATE the separate database nodes smoothly.
mnemonic.story_zh: 為了使系統「完整（INTEGR）」，工程師必須將獨立的資料庫節點順暢地「整合（INTEGRATE）」起來。
mnemonic.root_memory: INTEGR / INTEGER = whole, untouched, complete; connect this root idea with integrate.

example: Immigrants often face significant cultural barriers when trying to integrate into a new society.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 integrate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: incorporate is related, but integrate has its own usage pattern and context.
merge may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with integrate.

usage_note: integrate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To explain the meaning of information, words, or actions; or to translate orally between distinct languages.
definition_zh: 詮釋；解釋；解讀；口譯

mnemonic.story_en: Acting INTER (between) two kings, the PRET (negotiator) had to INTERPRET the foreign message accurately.
mnemonic.story_zh: 站在兩位國王「之間（INTER）」，這位談判中間商（PRET）必須精確地「詮釋/口譯（INTERPRET）」這封外國信件。
mnemonic.root_memory: INTER = between, among; connect this root idea with interpret.

example: Data analysts are required to interpret complex data charts and present actionable summaries to executives.

roots.meaning_zh: 交易者、中間商、說明價值者

example_zh: 這個例句展示 interpret 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: explain is related, but interpret has its own usage pattern and context.
decode may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with interpret.

usage_note: interpret is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To show or prove to be right, reasonable, or warranted under critical scrutiny.
definition_zh: 證明…是正當的；為…辯護；使合理化

mnemonic.story_en: The general had to perform actions to make the case JUST (correct) to JUSTIFY the invasion to the global media.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將軍必須採取行動讓理由顯得「正確（JUST）」，以此向全球媒體「證明（JUSTIFY）」這場入侵的正當性。
mnemonic.root_memory: JUST / JUS = law, right, correct; connect this root idea with justify.

example: The high cost of the medical equipment is justified by the thousands of lives it saves annually.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 justify 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: legitimize is related, but justify has its own usage pattern and context.
warrant may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with justify.

usage_note: justify is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Conforming to the law or to rules; legal, lawful, or able to be defended as reasonable and valid.
definition_zh: 合法的；正當的；合理的；正統的

mnemonic.story_en: The business operates within strict LEG (law) frameworks, ensuring all its profits are perfectly LEGITIMATE.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這家企業在嚴格的「法律（LEG）」框架內運作，確保其所有利潤完全是「合法的（LEGITIMATE）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: LEG / LEX = law; connect this root idea with legitimate.

example: The customer had a legitimate grievance regarding the defective battery, so the retail shop issued a full refund.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 legitimate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: lawful is related, but legitimate has its own usage pattern and context.
valid may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with legitimate.

usage_note: legitimate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To display or show a quality or feeling by one's acts or appearance; to demonstrate clearly.
definition_zh: 顯現；流露；表明；展現

mnemonic.story_en: The symptom became so clear it felt like it could be seized by a MANUS (hand), starting to MANIFEST on his skin.
mnemonic.story_zh: 症狀變得如此清晰，彷彿可以用「手（MANUS）」去抓住，開始在皮膚上「顯現（MANIFEST）」出來。
mnemonic.root_memory: MANUS = hand; connect this root idea with manifest.

example: Deep psychological stress can often manifest itself as physical symptoms like chronic migraines.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 manifest 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: display is related, but manifest has its own usage pattern and context.
exhibit may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with manifest.

usage_note: manifest is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To handle or control something tool or variable with skill; or to control or influence a person or situation cleverly or unfairly.
definition_zh: 操縱；控制；熟練地操作；在背後控制（人）

mnemonic.story_en: With his MANUS (hand) filling the control room, the technician could MANIPULATE the complex robotic arms.
mnemonic.story_zh: 「手（MANUS）」中握滿了控制權，技術人員便能靈活地「操縱（MANIPULATE）」複雜的機械手臂。
mnemonic.root_memory: MANUS = hand; connect this root idea with manipulate.

example: The dictator used state-controlled television networks to manipulate public opinion during the election.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 manipulate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: maneuver is related, but manipulate has its own usage pattern and context.
influence may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with manipulate.

usage_note: manipulate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Relating to or at the edge or margin; minimal, minor, or barely sufficient.
definition_zh: 邊緣的；微小的；不重要的；邊際的

mnemonic.story_en: The editor scribbled minor notes on the MARGO (edge) of the paper, representing MARGINAL corrections.
mnemonic.story_zh: 編輯在紙張的「邊緣（MARGO）」塗寫了小筆記，這代表了「微小的（MARGINAL）」修正。
mnemonic.root_memory: MARGO = border, edge, brink; connect this root idea with marginal.

example: The new advertising campaign resulted in only a marginal increase in total monthly sales.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 marginal 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: slight is related, but marginal has its own usage pattern and context.
minimal may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with marginal.

usage_note: marginal is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To make partial or minor changes to something, typically to improve it or make it more suitable for a specific purpose.
definition_zh: 修改；更改；修正；（文法）修飾

mnemonic.story_en: The mechanics had to make the engine fit the standard MOD (measure) to MODIFY the sports car for racing rules.
mnemonic.story_zh: 技工必須讓引擎符合規格「限度（MOD）」，以此「修改（MODIFY）」跑車以符合賽事規則。
mnemonic.root_memory: MOD / MODUS = measure, limit, manner; connect this root idea with modify.

example: The architect agreed to modify the building plans to incorporate a wider elevator shaft.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 modify 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: alter is related, but modify has its own usage pattern and context.
amend may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with modify.

usage_note: modify is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To try to reach an agreement or compromise through formal discussion and bargaining with others.
definition_zh: 談判；協商；交涉

mnemonic.story_en: Merchants have NEG (no) time for OT (leisure) when they must sit at the table and NEGOTIATE the trade contract.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當商家必須坐在桌前「談判（NEGOTIATE）」貿易合約時，他們「不（NEG）」可能有「閒暇（OT）」時間。
mnemonic.root_memory: NEG = not; connect this root idea with negotiate.

example: The labor union is currently meeting with management to negotiate a higher base salary for workers.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 negotiate 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: bargain is related, but negotiate has its own usage pattern and context.
arbitrate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with negotiate.

usage_note: negotiate is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Not influenced by personal feelings, interpretations, or prejudice; based completely on unbiased facts.
definition_zh: 客觀的；真實的；（名詞）目標

mnemonic.story_en: The judge looked at the evidence OB (in front) ject thrown down, remaining strictly OBJECTIVE in her verdict.
mnemonic.story_zh: 法官看著「扔（JECT）」在自己「面前（OB）」的證據，在判決中保持了絕對「客觀的（OBJECTIVE）」態度。
mnemonic.root_memory: OB = against, toward, in front of; connect this root idea with objective.

example: A journalist has a professional duty to provide an objective report of the political rally.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 objective 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: unbiased is related, but objective has its own usage pattern and context.
impartial may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with objective.

usage_note: objective is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Not discovered or known about; uncertain, or difficult to see, express, or understand clearly.
definition_zh: 鮮為人知的；晦澀的；模糊的；遮掩

mnemonic.story_en: Clouds came OB (over) and left the mountain peak SCUR (covered), making the trail highly OBSCURE.
mnemonic.story_zh: 烏雲籠罩在「之上（OB）」並將山頂「覆蓋（SCUR）」，使得山路變得非常「模糊不清（OBSCURE）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: OB = over, thoroughly; connect this root idea with obscure.

example: The academic journal article was filled with obscure references that only a few historians could identify.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 obscure 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: vague is related, but obscure has its own usage pattern and context.
ambiguous may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with obscure.

usage_note: obscure is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: A seemingly absurd or self-contradictory statement or proposition that when investigated or explained may prove to be well founded or true.
definition_zh: 悖論；似非而是的說法；矛盾的人事物

mnemonic.story_en: The speaker voiced an opinion PARA (contrary to) the public DOXA (belief), introducing a fascinating PARADOX.
mnemonic.story_zh: 演講者提出了與公眾「信念（DOXA）」「相反（PARA）」的觀點，引入了一個迷人的「悖論（PARADOX）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: PARA = contrary to, beside; connect this root idea with paradox.

example: It is a strange paradox that some of the world's richest countries contain pockets of extreme poverty.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 paradox 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: contradiction is related, but paradox has its own usage pattern and context.
anomaly may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with paradox.

usage_note: paradox is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Seeming reasonable, believable, or probable, even if not fully proven true yet.
definition_zh: 似合理的；可信的；說得通的

mnemonic.story_en: The alibi sounded so strong it deserved a PLAUS (applause), marking it as a PLAUSIBLE theory.
mnemonic.story_zh: 這套不在場證明聽起來非常有道理，值得「鼓掌（PLAUS）認可」，是一個「可信的（PLAUSIBLE）」說法。
mnemonic.root_memory: PLAUS / PLAUDERE = to clap, applaud, approve; connect this root idea with plausible.

example: The detective noted that while the suspect's story was plausible, it lacked physical evidence.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 plausible 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: credible is related, but plausible has its own usage pattern and context.
believable may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with plausible.

usage_note: plausible is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a way that is based on practical rather than theoretical considerations.
definition_zh: 務實的；重實效的；實用主義的

mnemonic.story_en: Instead of reading pure philosophy, the CEO focused on the PRAGMA (deed) to take a PRAGMATIC step.
mnemonic.story_zh: 與其閱讀純粹的哲學理論，執行長更專注於「具體行動（PRAGMA）」，採取「務實的（PRAGMATIC）」步驟。
mnemonic.root_memory: PRAGMA = deed, act, concrete matter; connect this root idea with pragmatic.

example: The two countries set aside historical grievances to forge a pragmatic economic partnership.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 pragmatic 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: practical is related, but pragmatic has its own usage pattern and context.
realistic may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with pragmatic.

usage_note: pragmatic is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To prevent from happening; to make something impossible, especially by taking action in advance.
definition_zh: 排除；防止；使不可能；杜絕

mnemonic.story_en: The guard will PRE (before) clude danger by slamming the gate CLUD (shut) to PRECLUDE illegal entry.
mnemonic.story_zh: 警衛藉由「提前（PRE）」「關上（CLUD）」大門來阻擋危險，以「杜絕（PRECLUDE）」非法進入。
mnemonic.root_memory: PRE = before; connect this root idea with preclude.

example: A pre-existing medical condition does not automatically preclude you from buying travel insurance.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 preclude 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: prevent is related, but preclude has its own usage pattern and context.
obviate may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with preclude.

usage_note: preclude is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quality of something (its traits and features) rather than its raw numeric quantity.
definition_zh: 性質的；質化的；質性的

mnemonic.story_en: Researchers check the basic QUAL (kind) of behavior during a QUALITATIVE interview rather than counting digits.
mnemonic.story_zh: 研究人員在進行「質性（QUALITATIVE）」訪談時，會檢查行為的內在「屬性（QUAL）」而不是計算數字。
mnemonic.root_memory: QUAL / QUALIS = of what kind, property; connect this root idea with qualitative.

example: The sociology department prefers qualitative research methods, such as open-ended focus groups, over statistical surveys.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 qualitative 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: descriptive is related, but qualitative has its own usage pattern and context.
subjective may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with qualitative.

usage_note: qualitative is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Not or no longer needed or useful; superfluous, or repeating data unnecessarily; (UK/corporate) laid off from a job because the position is no longer required.
definition_zh: 多餘的；贅述的；被裁員的

mnemonic.story_en: When water flows RE (again) as an extra UND (wave), the glass overflows and becomes REDUNDANT.
mnemonic.story_zh: 當水流「再次（RE）」形成多餘的「波浪（UND）」時，杯子就溢出來了，變得「多餘的（REDUNDANT）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: RE = again, back; connect this root idea with redundant.

example: Writing 'free gift' is grammatically redundant because all gifts are inherently free.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 redundant 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: superfluous is related, but redundant has its own usage pattern and context.
unnecessary may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with redundant.

usage_note: redundant is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: To strengthen or support an existing structure, feeling, habit, or military force with additional material or personnel.
definition_zh: 加強；增援；強化（觀念或結構）

mnemonic.story_en: The general sent units RE (again) IN (into) the field to bring extra FORC (strength) to REINFORCE the broken line.
mnemonic.story_zh: 將軍「再次（RE）」將部隊派「入（IN）」戰場，帶來額外的「力量（FORC）」以「增援/加強（REINFORCE）」斷裂的防線。
mnemonic.root_memory: RE = again; connect this root idea with reinforce.

example: The teacher used positive rewards, like gold stars, to reinforce good behavior in the classroom.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 reinforce 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: strengthen is related, but reinforce has its own usage pattern and context.
bolster may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with reinforce.

usage_note: reinforce is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.

definition: Closely connected or appropriate to what is being done, discussed, or considered at that moment.
definition_zh: 相關的；切題的；有重大關係的

mnemonic.story_en: The speaker chose to RE (again) LEV (lift) the primary data point because it was highly RELEVANT to the debate.
mnemonic.story_zh: 演講者選擇「再次（RE）」「抬高舉起（LEV）」核心數據，因為這與辯論主題「高度相關（RELEVANT）」。
mnemonic.root_memory: RE = again, back; connect this root idea with relevant.

example: Please include all relevant work experience on your resume when applying for the senior managerial role.
example_zh: 這個例句展示 relevant 在正式語境中的自然用法。

near_synonyms.difference: applicable is related, but relevant has its own usage pattern and context.
germane may overlap in meaning, but it is not always interchangeable with relevant.

usage_note: relevant is common in college-level academic or professional English; check collocations for natural use.
